task.description: Bring the page to life. 1) A click on #like-btn increases the number in #like-count by 1. 2) A click on #theme-toggle toggles the class theme-dark on body and sets the button's aria-pressed to "true" or "false". 3) One handler on #faq (delegation): a click on .faq__question shows or hides the .faq__answer of its own .faq__item and updates aria-expanded. 4) Escape on the page closes all answers and sets aria-expanded="false". 5) Typing in #comment writes "12 / 100" into #comment-counter. Only addEventListener; do not use onclick, innerHTML or element.style.

tests.name: One click on "Like" → 1
tests.fail: In the handler increase likes and write it into #like-count: likeCount.textContent = String(likes);

tests.name: Three clicks → 3
tests.check: (() => { const b = document.querySelector("#like-btn"); b.click(); b.click(); b.click(); return document.querySelector("#like-count").textContent === "3"; })()
tests.fail: Declare let likes = 0; OUTSIDE the handler, otherwise counting starts over every time.

tests.name: Theme: one click turns on theme-dark and aria-pressed="true"
tests.check: (() => { const b = document.querySelector("#theme-toggle"); b.click(); return document.body.classList.contains("theme-dark") && b.getAttribute("aria-pressed") === "true"; })()

tests.name: Theme: a second click turns it off
tests.check: (() => { const b = document.querySelector("#theme-toggle"); b.click(); b.click(); return !document.body.classList.contains("theme-dark") && b.getAttribute("aria-pressed") === "false"; })()

tests.name: A click on a question opens the answer and sets aria-expanded="true"
tests.fail: Find the answer of its own block: question.closest(".faq__item").querySelector(".faq__answer").

tests.name: A second click closes the answer
tests.fail: Toggle: answer.hidden = !answer.hidden and aria-expanded from the new state.

tests.name: A click on a span inside the button works too
tests.fail: event.target can be a nested element - use event.target.closest(".faq__question").

tests.name: A question added after loading works (delegation)
tests.check: (() => { const item = document.createElement("div"); item.className = "faq__item"; const q = document.createElement("button"); q.type = "button"; q.className = "faq__question"; q.setAttribute("aria-expanded", "false"); q.textContent = "New?"; const a = document.createElement("p"); a.className = "faq__answer"; a.hidden = true; a.textContent = "Yes"; item.append(q, a); document.querySelector("#faq").append(item); q.click(); return a.hidden === false && q.getAttribute("aria-expanded") === "true"; })()
tests.fail: Attach ONE handler to #faq, not one per button: then new questions work too.

tests.name: A click on the "Questions" heading breaks nothing
tests.fail: If the click is not on a question, closest returns null - leave the handler: if (!question) { return; }

tests.name: Escape closes all answers
tests.check: (() => { document.querySelectorAll(".faq__question")[0].click(); document.querySelectorAll(".faq__question")[1].click(); document.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key: "Escape", bubbles: true })); return [...document.querySelectorAll(".faq__answer")].every((a) => a.hidden) && [...document.querySelectorAll(".faq__question")].every((q) => q.getAttribute("aria-expanded") === "false"); })()

tests.name: Other keys do not close the answers
tests.check: (() => { document.querySelectorAll(".faq__question")[0].click(); document.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent("keydown", { key: "Enter", bubbles: true })); return document.querySelectorAll(".faq__answer")[0].hidden === false; })()

tests.name: Character counter: "JavaScript" → "10 / 100"
tests.check: (() => { const c = document.querySelector("#comment"); c.value = "JavaScript"; c.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); return document.querySelector("#comment-counter").textContent === "10 / 100"; })()

tests.name: The program runs without errors
tests.fail: A null error - check the selectors.

hints: Like counter: let likes = 0; outside the handler.
classList.toggle returns true if the class was added: const isDark = document.body.classList.toggle("theme-dark");
aria attributes are strings: setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(isDark)).
Delegation: faq.addEventListener("click", (event) => { const question = event.target.closest(".faq__question"); if (!question) { return; } ... });
The answer of its own block: question.closest(".faq__item").querySelector(".faq__answer")

wrong_solutions.mistake: the counter is declared inside the handler
a handler on every button instead of delegation
the counter uses the change event

questions.question: Which line correctly subscribes the button btn to clicks?
questions.explanation: The function is passed without parentheses; the event type is a string.

questions.question: Why is the page always showing 1 when let likes = 0; is inside the handler?
options: The variable is created anew with zero on every click
textContent does not work with numbers
questions.explanation: State is stored outside the handler.

questions.question: Which property of the event object holds the element the event happened on? Type event.<property>.
questions.explanation: event.target is the deepest element that was clicked.

questions.question: Match the event with the moment.
pairs: Every change of a field's value
questions.explanation: The event type is the first argument of addEventListener.

questions.question: How do you check that the Escape key was pressed?
questions.explanation: event.key is the name of the key.

questions.question: What does event.preventDefault() do in a click handler on a link?
questions.explanation: The browser's default action is cancelled.

questions.question: What is event bubbling?
options: The event rises from the target element to its parents
The event passes to sibling elements
questions.explanation: That is why a click on a button can be caught on its container.

questions.question: What advantages does event delegation give?
options: It works for elements added later
No need to check what was clicked

questions.question: Why event.target.closest(".item") in delegation and not just event.target?
options: The click may come from a nested element (span, icon); closest finds the .item itself
questions.explanation: closest searches from the element itself up through its parents.

questions.question: Which choices make an expanding section accessible?
questions.explanation: A div does not get focus and cannot be pressed from the keyboard.

questions.question: What value does String(true) give? Type it.
questions.explanation: aria attributes are strings, so values are converted with String().

questions.question: Why does the course not use the onclick="..." attribute?
options: It mixes code with markup; handlers live in the JS file
questions.explanation: Like style="" in CSS: we keep HTML and behaviour apart.
